title: Signed width-$l$ DNF for a depth-$\le 1$ gate over subcircuits
statement: Fix natural numbers $m,n,l$. Let $c_j$ be a Boolean circuit whose $m$ inputs are indexed by $\mathrm{Fin}\,m$ and whose depth is at most $1$, and let $\mathrm{gates}$ assign to each index $i \in \mathrm{Fin}\,m$ a Boolean function $\mathrm{gates}_i \colon (\mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \bbf_2) \to \bbf_2$. Suppose that every $\mathrm{gates}_i$ is computed by some DNF over $n$ variables of width at most $l$, and also by some CNF over $n$ variables of width at most $l$. Then there exist a DNF $\varphi$ over $n$ variables of width at most $l$ and a sign bit $s \in \mathrm{Bool}$ such that, for every assignment $x \colon \mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \bbf_2$, the value $\varphi$ takes at $x$ when $s = \mathrm{true}$, and its negation when $s = \mathrm{false}$, equals the value of $c_j$ under the assignment $i \mapsto \mathrm{gates}_i(x)$; moreover, each term of $\varphi$ contains no repeated literal, and no two of its literals share a variable.
hypotheses_covered: each gate function $\mathrm{gates}_i$ has a DNF of width $\le l$
each gate function $\mathrm{gates}_i$ has a CNF of width $\le l$
replaced:
A circuit $c_j$ of depth at most $1$ over gates that each have a width-$l$ DNF and CNF
representation admits a width-$l$ DNF $\varphi$ together with a sign bit such that, for
all $x$, the signed evaluation $\big(\mathrm{if}\ \mathit{sign}\ \mathrm{then}\
\varphi.\mathrm{eval}\,x\ \mathrm{else}\ \neg\varphi.\mathrm{eval}\,x\big)$ equals
$c_j.\mathrm{eval}\,(\lambda i,\ \mathrm{gates}\,i\,x)$; moreover the terms of $\varphi$
are duplicate-free with no repeated variable.
